answer: Rate-limited reputation accrual resists sybils: an identity's reputation can only INCREASE by a small bounded amount per epoch regardless of how much work it floods in, so reputation is fundamentally time-gated. A river of fakes cannot buy standing with a burst of activity — each is capped at the slow per-epoch accrual, and the vertex of full reputation is many epochs away. A thread of honest agents accrues steadily; an attacker needs every fake to age through the same slow reputation ramp, so instant mass creation yields instant mass IRRELEVANCE until the epochs pass.
